scenes.title: Where and when
narration: Leventikos is a traditional dance rooted in western Macedonia, practiced by Slav Macedonians and Greeks across Florina, Resen, and Bitola.
It shares historical musical ties with Balkan ballads and regional dance forms.

scenes.title: Listen
narration: Music is built on asymmetric meters of 12/8 (3+2+2+3+2) and 16/8 (4+2+3+4+3).
Tunes like Ibraim Odza are performed in multiple metric variations, sharing rhythmic space with dances like Pušteno and Beranče.
The pulse is 12/8 and 16/8 asymmetric.
Asymmetric Balkan dance tunes featuring shifting accents across five irregular beats, with ornamented melodies adaptable to both 12/8 and 16/8 time signatures.

scenes.title: The people
narration: The dance performed in Petroussa is very different from the one in Florina.
Classified as a subclass of the hora dance family, sharing metric structures with regional tunes like Berace, Beranče, Bajrače, and Pušteno.
on_screen: Names on screen as they are spoken
Variant names as a small list

scenes.title: Family tree
narration: Leventikos is variant of Pušteno: Shares performance tunes and similar 16/8 metric interpretations.
Leventikos is shares music of Beranče: Utilizes the traditional 12/8 (3+2+2+3+2) meter.
Leventikos is parent of Hora: Classified within the broader hora circle dance family.

music_brief.rights_rule: A composition brief does not clear an output. Record the provider/model/version, terms and date, input rights, output licence, restrictions and review before release.
music_brief.sound_description: Asymmetric Balkan dance tunes featuring shifting accents across five irregular beats, with ornamented melodies adaptable to both 12/8 and 16/8 time signatures.
music_brief.prompt: Original instrumental composition in the musical world of Leventikos (Greece and North Macedonia). Meter 12/8 and 16/8 asymmetric. Rhythm pattern: 3+2+2+3+2 or 4+2+3+4+3. Mood: lively, asymmetric, traditional. It should sound like this: Asymmetric Balkan dance tunes featuring shifting accents across five irregular beats, with ornamented melodies adaptable to both 12/8 and 16/8 time signatures. New melody, new arrangement: do not quote or imitate any specific recorded song; keep the idiom, the instruments, the pulse and the proportions.
